description: Runs the validation of every tag, alarm, connection and screen (with its items) of a WinCC Unified HMI, as far as the scope selects, and lists what it reports as {hmi, scope, checked:{tags, alarms, connections, screens, screenItems}, errors, warnings, findings:[{objectKind, object, property, errors, warnings}], total, nextCursor, inventoryGaps}. This is NOT a compile: the V21 API has none for Unified, so no result says the HMI compiles, and `checked` counts the objects that were validated (0 for a scope not selected). Use it after tag or alarm writes, which do not scan screens, scripts or logging for references. errors and warnings count the WHOLE result, not the page; a finding is one object property with at least one error or warning, and a validation that threw is a finding with property null plus an inventoryGaps entry. `scope` is all (default), tags, alarms, connections or screens. A big HMI can take minutes: narrow with scope. For a large HMI read it in pages: pass limit (1-1000), then pass the nextCursor of each page as cursor until nextCursor is null; total is the number of findings of the whole list. Without limit and cursor the whole list is returned with nextCursor null. A cursor of a list that changed is 409 cursor_stale (restart without cursor), one that is not a nextCursor is 400 invalid_cursor. `inventoryGaps` [{kind, subject, reason}] lists every value or object the serve could not read while building the answer (empty when all reads succeeded): the unreadable value is null and one gap names it, so a null next to a gap means unreadable, while a value the object does not offer is null without a gap. Needs an open project and a WinCC Unified HMI (hmi = its name from tia_hmis, matched ignoring case): a classic WinCC HMI is refused with 409 hmi_not_unified, an unknown HMI is 404 not_found and two HMIs with the same name are 409 ambiguous_name. Maps to GET /hmi/{hmi}/validate?scope=&limit=&cursor= (all optional). Read-only (class R). Long operation: may answer status:"running" + jobId — then call tia_job_status.

cursor.description: the nextCursor of the previous page, passed back exactly as received; it is opaque, so never invent, build or edit one (omit it for the first page, and omit both limit and cursor for the whole list)

hmi.description: HMI name, as listed by tia_hmis (a WinCC Unified HMI)

limit.description: page size, an integer from 1 to 1000; pass it to read the list in pages (omit both limit and cursor for the whole list)

scope.description: what to validate: all (default), tags, alarms, connections or screens

name: tia_hmi_validate
title: TIA — validate a HMI Unified
